## Why visit

The strongest rural-inn contrast to Liverpool’s ornate city pubs: thatch, exposed structural timbers, plain benches and small rooms arranged around fireplaces. It is worth the excursion for the atmosphere of an older country drinking place, particularly when November weather makes an indoor stop attractive. The pub’s famous medieval origin story needs care: CAMRA’s detailed heritage account discusses timber dating around the mid-sixteenth century and treats earlier pub-use claims cautiously. The observable building and rooms are impressive without turning folklore into verified history.
